{"self_assessment": "Impact
I designed the fish on the scratch pad: nose on the left, two body lines splitting from a single start, crossing at the tail neck and flaring into a fork. That design gave us a recognizable animal outline that one push could run through. Once the start moved to the nose, the whole structure was connected, and by our last check all 111 standing dominoes were linked to the start. I also laid a large share of the bottom body line and carried the line on from the crossing out toward the upper fork tip.

Execution
I traced the bottom stroke from the nose and kept laying it in steady batches. I inspected the crossing and joints twice, at the midpoint and again once the lines had come through, to confirm the fall would pass cleanly. I chose not to add extra back-half strokes, because each one would add another joint that could break. In the last minutes I kept my hands off the crossing so we did not risk a bump, and the picture stayed intact up to the push.

Collaboration
I kept the table informed throughout. I assigned strokes, handed the lagging bottom run to Tom while I checked the joints behind him, and picked the line back up at the crossing for the final stretch to the upper tip. I answered Priya's and Leo's questions about the pad and the start position directly. I also coordinated hand positions so we did not collide.

Leadership
I set the plan early: who traced which stroke, where the start went, and when to stop touching the build. I made the call to keep the single-start, two-line design and to keep hands off before the push. I kept the team's attention on the clock.", "my_share_percent": 35}
